subject: Renewal: phased commit with surge protection + evaluation credits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mills <sara.mills@omnicare.io>, procurement@omnicare.io
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: phased commit with surge protection + evaluation credits

Hi Sara / OmniCare procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive renewal call yesterday. As promised, attaching a concise proposal designed to give you predictability on pricing while keeping room to scale during your seasonal peak. High-level summary: 

- 12-month renewal term starting 2028-07-01
- Staged commit: 60% of prior-year commit for Q3 (safety month), ramping to 100% in Q4
- Surge protection pool: 15% burst capacity available at a negotiated overage rate (applies automatically)
- Evaluation credits: 250k token credit for ramp testing and validation during first 60 days
- 10% list discount applied to committed usage; overages billed at 60% of list with monthly true-up

I've attached the SOW and the usage forecast we discussed. Ben (copied) added a short performance addendum to lock latency SLOs for your V2 inference pipelines. Vivek — I’ve flagged this with you because they asked about a limited price-hold for the first month of their Q4 marketing surge; if we can approve a short price-hold that would smooth legal and procurement.

Next steps: please confirm the model of commitment you prefer (accept staged ramp vs. flat commit), and we’ll draft the amendment for signatures. Happy to hop on a quick call Thursday if useful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: OmniCare_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW, pricing table), usage-forecast-q3-q4.csv (forecast)
From: Sara Mills <sara.mills@omnicare.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@omnicare.io, Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@omnicare.io>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 12:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: phased commit with surge protection + evaluation credits

Marissa,

Appreciate the clear summary and the attachments. A few quick clarifications from procurement and engineering after an internal read: 

1) Procurement would like a 60-day price-hold on committed unit pricing starting at Q4 kickoff (we need to lock marketing forecasts by then). Is that something you can commit to in the amendment?
2) Engineering asked whether the 250k evaluation credit can be used against inference for both hosted and our private VPC deployment (we will run split tests).
3) Can you confirm the overage rate calc? We want a simple cap we can audit on invoices.

If those items are explicit in the amendment we can move forward quickly. We’d like to keep the staged ramp (60% then 100%), assuming the price-hold is accepted.

Thanks,
Sara
Sr. Procurement Manager | OmniCare
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mills <sara.mills@omnicare.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, procurement@omnicare.io
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: phased commit with surge protection + evaluation credits

Hi Sara — thanks for the quick review, and great questions. Responses below (and I’ve highlighted the items we need legal to reflect in the amendment):

1) Price-hold: yes, we can offer a one-month price-hold on committed unit pricing at Q4 kickoff (2028-10-01 to 2028-10-31). Operational notes: the price-hold applies only to committed unit pricing (not discounts on overage tiers), and it will be documented as a time-bound amendment clause. Vivek, can you confirm executive approval for the price-hold as described?

2) Evaluation credits: confirmed — the 250k token credit can be applied across both Hosted and Private (VPC) deployments. We’ll add a short usage policy to the SOW so it’s reproducible for audits.

3) Overage rate: overages will be billed at 60% of list price per-token, with a monthly true-up capped at the surge protection pool (15% of committed monthly tokens). We’ll include a worked example in the amendment and a link to invoice calculations. For auditability, we’ll add a per-invoice line item showing committed_units, consumed_committed, consumed_overage, and applied_burst.

Attached: small performance addendum from Ben (ben, thanks) and a redlined pricing table. If OmniCare is comfortable, next step would be legal to route the amendment for signature; I’ve copied procurement so they can confirm timing.

Proposed timeline: you confirm acceptance of price-hold and staged ramp by end of week (5/19), legal review the week of 5/22, signature target 6/05, term effective 7/01.

Best,
Marissa

--- Original attachment: pricing-addendum-ben.docx (performance SLOs and latency targets)
From: Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@omnicare.io>

Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: phased commit with surge protection + evaluation credits

Marissa / Marissa team,

All sounds good from legal and procurement — we reviewed the clarifications and the one-month price-hold as written is acceptable. Two operational asks before signature: 

- Please include the worked overage example in the amendment (makes invoicing simpler).
- Can Ben add a short paragraph in the SLO addendum about incident escalation during the Q4 surge window (we need a named contact + 30-min response target for Sev1).

If you include those, I’ll route to our CFO for final sign-off and we’ll plan for DocuSign the week of 6/05. Appreciate the flexibility on the split-use evaluation credits.

Thanks,
Daniel Ortiz
Director, Cloud Ops | OmniCare
